discovery: Controlled/living radical polymerization (atom transfer radical polymerization), which enables precise synthesis of well-defined polymers and functional materials
rationale: ATRP changed polymer synthesis. It made it possible to control molecular weight, architecture and end-group functionality. It is now used throughout materials science, coatings, biomedicine and nanotechnology. Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto independently published the metal-catalyzed controlled radical polymerization in 1995 and have long been cited as leading candidates; each has received the Wolf Prize or a comparable award. The Chemistry prize has recently gone to biology-related work (2024) and to framework materials (2025), so a synthetic polymer chemistry prize fits the rotation pattern.
